key: The valley spirit dies not, aye the same; The female mystery thus do we name.
s: The chapter opens here, then turns to a gate and root; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 6, reads the valley as nourishing the spirits of the five viscera, and the female mystery as heaven and earth, in a person the nose and mouth.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 6, zh.wikisource, revision 2019760 (2021)

opened.locator: chapter 6 (title 成象), comments on 谷神不死 and 是謂玄牝
opened.edition: zh.wikisource 老子河上公章句, revision 2019760 (a normalised text)

evidence.words: 谷，養也。人能養神則不死也。神，謂五臟之神也。 … 玄，天也，於人為鼻。牝，地也，於人為口。
evidence.gloss: The valley means nourishing. If a person can nourish the spirits he does not die; the spirits are the spirits of the five viscera. … The dark is heaven, which in a person is the nose; the female is earth, which in a person is the mouth.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: The problem holds: the old plain sense restated the key verse (the valley spirit does not die, is named the female mystery). Rewritten to rules 1 and 2: the plain sense now gives only context (the verse opens the chapter, which then turns to a gate and a root), with no four-word run of the key verse. The reading keeps the Heshang Gong commentary and its glosses on 谷神不死 and 是謂玄牝, shortened to fit 45 words: the valley as nourishing the spirits of the five viscera (谷，養也 … 神，謂五臟之神也), and the female mystery as heaven and earth, in a person nose and mouth (玄，天也，於人為鼻。牝，地也，於人為口). The clause on heaven and earth feeding a person is dropped for length, not contradicted; nothing now goes beyond the quoted words. Key, ref, at and src unchanged. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 6, at [5]); entry-check ok, no warns; 44 words.
